title: Frock Catalog
description: FrockBot's own A2UI components. Drawn by the host from the app's own theme; a Bot or a Plugin composes them, and neither supplies code.

StatusPill.description: A small pill stating what state the card is in. One per card, beside its title.

label.description: The words on the pill, e.g. 'Ready to send' or 'Sent'. Bind this to the data model when the card settles.

tone.description: What the state means, which is what the host colours the pill by. 'ready' is waiting on the person, 'success' is done, 'warning' needs attention, 'danger' failed. Defaults to 'neutral'.

KeyValueRows.description: Labelled values in a column, one per row: From, To, Cc, Subject. For facts about the thing the card shows, never as a form.

rows.description: The rows, in the order they are read.

label.description: The short label on the left, e.g. 'To'.

value.description: The value on the right. Bind it to the data model when it changes.

CollapsibleText.description: A body of text that starts collapsed, with a control that shows the rest. For a draft, a quote, or anything longer than the card.

text.description: The body. Plain text; a card is not a document.

collapsedLines.description: How many lines are shown before the control appears. Defaults to 6.

ApprovalActions.description: The approve and decline controls for one Approval the kernel issued. Compose it into a card; the host draws the buttons and names the actions, and the decision is recorded once and durably.

approvalId.description: The id the kernel issued when the Bot proposed the action. A card cannot invent one: an id the kernel never recorded is refused when the button is pressed.

approveLabel.description: The word on the approving control. Defaults to 'Approve'.

declineLabel.description: The word on the declining control. Defaults to 'Decline'.

ConnectApp.description: An app from the Marketplace the person can connect: its logo, its name and a Connect button that opens the app's own sign-in. Name the app and nothing else; the host fills in the rest from its own catalog and draws the button, so a card can never say one app and connect another. A press never reaches you: the person signs in on the app's page, and the app's tools reach you on a later Turn.

app.description: The app: its Marketplace id, e.g. 'gmail' or 'googlecalendar', or its name, e.g. 'Google Calendar'. An app the Marketplace does not carry is refused when the card is sent, and the refusal names the closest ones it does.

name.description: Written by the host from its own catalog. Whatever a card puts here is replaced.

description.description: Written by the host from its own catalog. Whatever a card puts here is replaced.

packageId.description: Written by the host from its own catalog. Whatever a card puts here is replaced.

connectionTypeId.description: Written by the host from its own catalog. Whatever a card puts here is replaced.

Receipt.description: What a card settles into: its title, the pill saying what happened, and one line summarising it. Use it in place of the controls once the thing is done.

title.description: The same title the card carried before it settled.

status.description: The words on the pill, e.g. 'Sent'.

tone.description: What the state means. Defaults to 'success', because a receipt usually says a thing worked.

summary.description: One line saying what was done, e.g. 'Sent to nick@example.com — Re: Following up'.

MetricTile.description: One number that matters, with its name under it and an optional movement beside it. Put two or three in a Row for a summary; a Row of six is a table, so use DataTable instead.

label.description: What the number is, e.g. 'Open invoices'.

value.description: The number itself, already formatted the way a person reads it: '$4,120', '18%', '3 of 7'.

delta.description: How it moved, e.g. '+12%' or '-3 since Friday'. The host draws an arrow from the sign it starts with.

caption.description: One quiet line under the tile: the period, the source.

tone.description: What the number means — not which way it moved. Defaults to 'neutral'.

ProgressBar.description: A proportion: how far through something is, how much of a budget is used. For work that is running, not for a rating.

value.description: Between 0 and 1. Anything outside that is clamped. Bind it and the bar moves with one updateDataModel.

label.description: What is progressing, above the bar.

caption.description: The count in words, at the right of the label: '3 of 7', '62%'.

tone.description: What the host colours the filled part. Defaults to 'ready' while something is running.

indeterminate.description: True when the proportion is not known yet: the bar animates instead of filling. Defaults to false.

DataTable.description: Rows in aligned columns: line items, search results, a comparison. The host lays the columns out so they fit the card at phone width — never compose a table out of Rows.

columns.description: The columns, left to right. Five at most: a card is not a spreadsheet.

align.description: Which edge the cells sit against. Use 'end' for numbers. Defaults to 'start'.

weight.description: This column's share of the width, against the other columns'. Defaults to 1.

rows.description: The rows, in the order they are read. A row has one cell per column; a short row is padded, and extra cells are dropped.

cells.description: This row's cells, in column order.

caption.description: One line under the table, e.g. 'Showing the 12 most recent of 340'. Say so here when the rows are a sample.

Timeline.description: What happened, in order, down a rail: the steps of a run, the history of a thread, what a Routine did overnight. For events with a time, not for a list of things.

entries.description: The events, oldest first unless the card says otherwise.

title.description: What happened, in a few words.

time.description: When, in the words a person reads: '9:14am', 'Tuesday', '3 days ago'.

tone.description: What this step means, which is what the host colours its dot. Defaults to 'neutral'.

ChoiceChips.description: Pick one of a handful of options, laid out as chips that wrap. For a short, visible set — a tone, a recipient, a date the Bot suggested. Use ChoicePicker for a long list.

options.description: What can be picked, in the order shown.

value.description: What is written to the data model when it is picked. This is what you will read back, so make it something you can act on.
Where the pick is kept: write a binding, `{"path": "/tone"}`. It must be a binding — a press carries the data model back, and a selection the component kept to itself would never reach you.

action.description: Raised as soon as a chip is picked, when picking is the whole answer. Leave it out when a Button below submits the card.

MultiSelect.description: Tick any number of a handful of options. The ticked values are kept as a list in the data model, in the order the options are declared.

options.description: What can be ticked, in the order shown.

value.description: What appears in the list when it is ticked.

detail.description: One quieter line under the label.

values.description: Where the ticked values are kept: write a binding, `{"path": "/include"}`. Seed the data model with the ones that start ticked.

maxSelected.description: How many may be ticked at once. Past it the unticked options stop responding and the host says why. Unbounded by default.

SegmentedControl.description: Choose between two, three or four things that are always visible — a view, a mode, a period. Not for an answer with many options: that is ChoiceChips.

label.description: The words in the segment. Keep them to one or two.

value.description: What is written to the data model when it is chosen.
Where the choice is kept: write a binding. The first segment is drawn as chosen when the data model holds nothing.

action.description: Raised when a segment is chosen. Leave it out when the choice only changes what the card shows.

Rating.description: How good was it, in stars. For asking, and — with readOnly — for showing a rating that is already recorded.

value.description: How many stars, from 0. Write a binding when you are asking; a literal is fine when readOnly is true.

max.description: How many stars there are. Defaults to 5.

label.description: What is being rated, drawn above the stars.

readOnly.description: True shows a rating rather than asking for one. Defaults to false.

ImageGallery.description: Several pictures in one component: what was found, what was generated, the pages of a document. One image draws full width; more than one draws as a strip that scrolls. Tapping one opens it.

images.description: The pictures, in the order they are shown.

url.description: An https:// image. A card carrying any other scheme is refused whole and nothing is drawn.

alt.description: What the picture shows, for a person who cannot see it. Write one.

FileAttachment.description: A file the card is about: a document, an export, a generated artifact. One row with what it is and a control that opens it.

name.description: The file's name, as the person would recognise it.

detail.description: What is worth knowing about it, already in words: 'PDF · 1.2 MB', 'Generated just now'. There is no formatting function; write the size the way a person reads it.

kind.description: What sort of file it is, which is the icon the host draws. Defaults to 'other'.

url.description: An https:// link to the file. With one the row offers to open it, through the app's own link handling; without one it is a row that says the file exists.

LinkPreview.description: One link, with enough of what is behind it that the person can decide before they follow it. Use it for a page a Bot found or made; a bare link inside prose belongs in Markdown.

url.description: Where it goes. https:// only, and the whole card is refused otherwise.

description.description: A line or two about it. Two lines at most are drawn.

site.description: Whose page it is, e.g. 'example.com'. Defaults to the link's own host.

imageUrl.description: An https:// thumbnail beside the title.

Markdown.description: A body of Markdown, drawn the way the Bot's own messages are: headings, bullet and ordered lists, emphasis, inline code, block quotes, rules and links. Use it for anything with structure in it; use Text for one plain run.

text.description: The Markdown source. The subset the app draws is the one it draws chat messages with; anything else is shown as the characters you wrote. No HTML is rendered, ever.

CodeBlock.description: Code, a command, or a payload, in a monospaced box with a control that copies it. Use it whenever the person might need the text exactly — never a Text, which will wrap and lose the indentation.

code.description: The text, exactly as it should be copied. Do not wrap it in backticks.

language.description: What it is, drawn as a label above the box: 'bash', 'json', 'dart'. There is no syntax colouring; this only says what the person is looking at.

caption.description: One line under the box: where it came from, what it does.

Quote.description: Something somebody else wrote, set apart from the card's own words: the message being replied to, the line of a document under discussion. Never for the Bot's own text.

text.description: The quoted words. Keep it to the part that matters; a long quotation belongs in CollapsibleText.

attribution.description: Who said it, and when: 'Nick, Tuesday 9:14am'.

CardHeader.description: The top of a card: its title, an optional line under it, and the pill saying what state it is in. Prefer this to a Row of Text and StatusPill — the host lays it out so the pill can never be pushed off the edge on a phone.

title.description: What the card is about, in a few words. Two lines at most; the host truncates past that.

subtitle.description: One quieter line under the title: who it is for, when it was made.

status.description: The words on the pill at the right, e.g. 'Ready to send'. Bind it to the data model and the card settles with one updateDataModel. Omit it for a card with no state.

tone.description: What the state means, which is what the host colours the pill by. Defaults to 'neutral'.

SectionHeader.description: A small heading that divides a long card into parts, with a hairline under it. Use it between blocks, never as the card's own title — that is CardHeader.

caption.description: A short note at the right of the heading, e.g. a count.

Callout.description: A tinted note beside the thing the card is about: a warning, a consequence, a piece of context. One per card at most — a card that needs two is telling the person too much at once.

text.description: What the person needs to know, in a sentence or two.

tone.description: What kind of note it is, which is what the host colours and which icon it draws. Defaults to 'neutral'.

IdentityRow.description: A person or an account on one line: an avatar, a name, and a quieter second line. For the sender of an email, the owner of a file, the account a connection belongs to.

detail.description: The second line: an address, a handle, a role.

imageUrl.description: An https:// avatar. A card carrying any other scheme is refused whole.

initials.description: What the avatar says when there is no image. Defaults to the first letter of the name.

id.description: A unique identifier for this component instance within the surface. This ID is used to refer to the component in layout children arrays or event handlers.
